source_verification_scope: Inspected the live page's text/snapshot, exact first-viewport screenshot, author-defined branch, published/updated labels, colophon and linked CC license. No live interaction or accessibility/performance testing.
observable_features: A single broad document column is dominated by large black sans-serif headings, followed by a smaller subtitle and linked author/update line.
A seven-item square-bulleted list uses blue underlined serif hyperlinks as visible navigation rather than image tiles or card components.
A thin horizontal rule and a second large section heading continue the document hierarchy on a pale neutral background.
No portrait, news photograph, advertisement, subscription form, saturated component fields or heavy boxed UI competes with the document structure in this viewport.
limits: A first viewport only: the rest of the published page contains a building photograph, example forms and a book promotion that are outside this capture. The site deliberately uses custom typography and CSS; do not call this screenshot browser-default or infer all direct Web Brutalism must use blue links, serif lists, large headings or this palette. No form controls are visible here. Author statements support this site's own design stance and colophon, not every web-brutalist designer's intent. A screenshot cannot prove keyboard operation, back behavior, DOM conformance, responsiveness, performance or the current appearance at another date/device.

association_evidence.supports: The author titles and frames this actual site as Guidelines for Brutalist Web Design, prioritizes raw content, readable documents, recognizable hyperlinks and controls, and explicitly says the site does not use default styles. Its colophon states hand-authored HTML, initial publication 4 April 2024, custom styling and fonts; the page shows an update label of 1 June 2025 and a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. The captured pixels, rather than the manifesto alone, supply the visible formal evidence.

Kate Moran's 2017 article distinguishes bare direct-document Web Brutalism from Antidesign and discusses historical functional precursors separately from later intentional trends. It supplies branch-comparison context; it does not identify or endorse this later Copeland page.

confusion_check.shared_appearances: Reduced decoration and plain document navigation overlap with minimal and legacy pages; large type alone is also widespread.
confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: Gumroad organizes a neobrutalist interface through heavy functional boundaries and flat color fields; the Copeland page uses a direct document hierarchy, exposed links and restrained chrome. These are distinct branches, not one mandatory recipe. A historical plain website or reduced palette alone does not establish deliberate Web Brutalism.
confusion_check.cannot_conclude: This authored example illustrates one branch. A plain old page is not automatically contemporary Web Brutalism; the screenshot does not establish Antidesign, site-wide interaction quality, performance or a universal style recipe.

selection_quality.subject_visibility: The actual page title, document hierarchy and all seven navigation links are readable at 1440×900.
selection_quality.unrelated_semantic_salience: No news/political portraits, dramatic headlines, generic subscription card or photograph appears in the first viewport.
selection_quality.scope: A representative authored direct-document branch only; retain Gumroad as a separate neobrutalist branch and do not merge their traits.
